name: Gaze Saccade Pattern Analysis
description: Analyzes saccadic eye movement patterns for physiological plausibility — AI faces lack natural micro-saccade dynamics.
mechanism:
This method detects deepfakes by analyzing the eye movement patterns — saccades, fixations, and micro-saccades — which follow strict neurophysiological laws that AI-generated faces cannot reproduce:

1. **Gaze Trajectory Extraction**: The method tracks iris and pupil positions across video frames using a high-precision eye region detector. Eye center positions are estimated from the visible iris contour using ellipse fitting (Świrski & Dodgson, 2013). The resulting gaze trajectory is decomposed into three movement types: (a) saccades — rapid ballistic eye movements (30–700°/s) that shift gaze between fixation targets, (b) fixations — stable gaze periods (200–400 ms typical duration) where the eye is relatively stationary, and (c) micro-saccades — involuntary miniature saccades (10–40 arcmin amplitude, 15–50°/s peak velocity) that occur during fixations. These movement types have distinct kinematic signatures that are neurologically constrained.

2. **Main Sequence Validation**: Real saccades obey the 'main sequence' — a fundamental law of oculomotor physiology: peak velocity scales linearly with saccade amplitude for small saccades (< 20°), following V_peak = 400–600 × amplitude (in °/s per degree). The duration-amplitude relationship follows T = 2.2 × A^0.4 (Baloh et al., 1975). The method fits these relationships to detected saccades and computes the R² goodness-of-fit. Authentic eyes produce R² > 0.85 for the main sequence. Deepfake eye movements — whether generated by the model or inherited from training data in an inconsistent temporal context — produce saccades that violate the main sequence: velocities may be too uniform, durations may not scale with amplitude, or the scatter around the main sequence regression may be too high.

3. **Micro-Saccade Statistics**: During fixation, real eyes produce involuntary micro-saccades at a rate of 1–3 per second, with amplitudes of 10–40 arcmin and characteristic velocity profiles (similar skewed Gaussian shape as large saccades). Micro-saccades follow the main sequence at their small amplitude range. The method measures: (a) micro-saccade rate — should be 1–3/s, (b) amplitude distribution — should be right-skewed with median 15–25 arcmin, (c) directional distribution — should show a bimodal pattern (predominantly horizontal), (d) temporal regularity — inter-micro-saccade intervals follow a gamma distribution. Deepfake eyes either show no micro-saccades (static during fixation), random jitter (uniform noise instead of ballistic micro-saccades), or micro-saccades with incorrect kinematic profiles.

4. **Blink-Saccade Coordination**: Physiologically, blinks and saccades are temporally coordinated — blinks tend to occur at saccade endpoints (gaze shift completion), and there is a refractory period of 100–200 ms after a saccade before a blink can occur. The method analyzes the temporal relationship between detected blinks and saccades, computing the cross-correlation function. Authentic video shows a peak in the blink probability at 50–200 ms after saccade offset. Deepfakes typically show random blink-saccade timing with no statistically significant correlation, as the neural networks generate blinks and eye movements as independent processes.
parameters:
Eye tracking: iris ellipse fitting at sub-pixel precision
Saccade detection: velocity threshold 30°/s (onset), 20°/s (offset)
Main sequence model: V_peak = k × amplitude, expected k = 400–600
Micro-saccade detection: velocity threshold 6°/s, minimum 6 ms duration
Micro-saccade rate: expected 1–3 per second
Fixation minimum duration: 100 ms
Blink-saccade correlation window: ±500 ms
Minimum video duration: 3 seconds
Minimum frame rate: 25 fps
Minimum eye resolution: 32×32 pixels
accuracy: 82–90% accuracy detecting deepfakes via gaze saccade analysis. Main sequence validation achieves AUC of 0.87 on FaceForensics++. Micro-saccade statistics provide F1-score of 0.84 when eye resolution is sufficient. Blink-saccade coordination adds 4–6% detection improvement. Performance requires sufficient video frame rate (≥ 25 fps) and eye resolution — low-resolution faces limit saccade detection precision.
source: Li, Y. et al. (2018). In Ictu Oculi: Exposing AI Created Fake Videos by Detecting Eye Blinking. Proceedings of IEEE WIFS, 1–7.
useCase: Detecting face swap and face reenactment deepfakes through eye movement analysis. Real-time liveness detection in video conferencing. Forensic analysis of talking-head video authenticity. Evaluating physiological plausibility of AI-generated video characters.
strengths:
• Based on fundamental neurophysiological laws that are difficult to fake
• Main sequence is a well-established quantitative relationship
• Micro-saccade analysis provides signal even during apparent stillness
• Blink-saccade coordination exploits neural coupling not modeled by generators
• Complementary to other face-based detection methods
limitations:
• Requires sufficient eye resolution and video frame rate
• Side-profile views or closed eyes eliminate the signal
• Some deepfake methods inherit eye dynamics from source video
• Subjects looking away from camera reduce gaze estimation accuracy
• Sunglasses, heavy makeup, or eye conditions affect analysis
